title: Top-degree module cohomology on a spectral ringed space restricts surjectively
statement: Let $T$ be a spectral topological space [def-weil-spectral-space], let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $T$, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer with $\dim T\leq d$ for topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$. For every quasi-compact open subset $W\subseteq T$, the canonical restriction map is surjective: $$H^d(T,F)\longrightarrow H^d(W,F|_W).$$ Here $F|_W$ and $\mathcal O|_W$ are ordinary restrictions to the open subspace, and cohomology is the right-derived global sections in all structure-sheaf modules, computed by injective resolutions [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. The restriction map is induced by restriction of sections on resolutions. No Noetherian, scheme, quasi-coherence, or coherence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A3G (proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral), part (2), with dimension bounded above by d; module form via Tag 01F1 (lemma-modules-abelian), part (1), whose common resolution identifies the restriction maps.

proof.text: If $T=\varnothing$ or $W=\varnothing$, the target section complex is zero, so surjectivity holds. Suppose $T\ne\varnothing$ and $d=0$. If $x$ specializes to $y\ne x$, sobriety makes $\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{x\}}$ a chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of length one, contradicting $\dim T\leq0$. Thus every point is closed. The set $T^c$ of closed points is therefore $T$, hence closed; clause (1) of [det-pe-wlocal-components] makes $T$ profinite, in particular Hausdorff. The quasi-compact open $W$ is closed, since a compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed. For $s\in H^0(W,F|_W)=F(W)$, glue $s$ and the zero section on the disjoint open complement $T\setminus W$. The result lies in $F(T)=H^0(T,F)$ and restricts to $s$. This proves degree zero without any assumption on the ring sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral, base case of (2); Topology Tag 0905 (lemma-characterize-profinite-spectral), via det-pe-wlocal-components clause (1).

proof.text: Write $A=F_{ab}$. On the site of opens of $T$ (a set of objects and arrows, taken in a common coefficient universe), apply [lem-sfb-ringed-sections-forget-abelian] with $B=\mathcal O$ and $K=F[0]$. It gives a derived isomorphism for every open $V$, natural for the actual restriction arrows. To read its source in the convention of the item, choose an injective module resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ using [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. It is bounded below and therefore K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. For each open $V$, its restriction is an injective resolution by [lem-sc-ringed-space-restrict-injective-resolution], so the source is represented by $\Gamma(V,I^\bullet)$. The comparison's target is derived abelian evaluation, equivalently global sections on the open subspace $V$. Applying degree-$d$ cohomology consequently gives additive bijections $c_V:H^d(V,F|_V)\to H^d(V,A|_V)$ in the ordinary injective-resolution conventions [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology, def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. For $V'\subseteq V$, naturality gives $c_{V'}\operatorname{res}^{F}_{V,V'}=\operatorname{res}^{A}_{V,V'}c_V$. This is an application of the cited derived isomorphism, not a claim that forgetting preserves injectivity.

source.place: Tag 01F1, lemma-modules-abelian (1), common-resolution comparison; Tag 01E1, lemma-cohomology-of-open. The existing derived-form comparison is sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded (2), including restriction naturality.

proof.text: Assume $d\geq1$ and let $\xi\in H^d(W,F|_W)$. Put $Z=T\setminus W$, $P=\{t\in T:\overline{\{t\}}\cap Z\ne\varnothing\}$ and $S=P\setminus Z$. The subset $Z$ is closed and its open complement is the given quasi-compact $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-punctured-spectral-neighborhood-dimension] with $n=d$: it gives that $S$ is spectral and $\dim S\leq d-1$, including the possibility that $S$ is empty. Apply [lem-sfb-spectral-space-cohomology-dimension] to the abelian sheaf $A|_S$ with dimension bound $d-1$ and cohomological degree $d>d-1$. Thus $H^d(S,A|_S)=0$. Here restriction to the possibly non-open $S$ means the inverse image along its subspace inclusion, as in the two cited statements. This uses only the vanishing statement of the dimension theorem, not its proof's top-degree surjectivity assertion.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, induction step proving (2), punctured generalization neighborhood and lower-dimensional vanishing; Topology Tag 0AP0, lemma-make-spectral-space-minus.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-punctured-neighborhood-cohomology-colimit] to $T,Z,A$ and $p=d$. All hypotheses hold by step 3: $Z$ is closed with quasi-compact open complement. Its small directed index is the set of quasi-compact open neighborhoods $N$ of $Z$, ordered by reverse inclusion; it contains $T$, and binary intersections give common later indices. The class $c_W(\xi)$ is at the stage $N=T$, since $T\setminus Z=W$. The canonical colimit comparison identifies its image with a class in $H^d(S,A|_S)=0$. By [lem-sc-filtered-colimit-map-zero] there is a quasi-compact open $N\supseteq Z$ such that $\operatorname{res}^{A}_{W,N\cap W}(c_W(\xi))=0$. Step 2 identifies this with $c_{N\cap W}(\operatorname{res}^{F}_{W,N\cap W}(\xi))$. Since $c_{N\cap W}$ is injective, $\xi$ restricts to zero in $H^d(N\cap W,F|_{N\cap W})$.

source.place: Tag 0A3D, lemma-cohomology-of-neighbourhoods-of-closed (2); Tag 0A3G, proof of (2), passage from the zero colimit class to a quasi-compact neighborhood.

proof.text: Since $N\supseteq Z=T\setminus W$, the opens $W,N$ cover $T$. Apply [lem-sc-mayer-vietoris-ringed-space] to $(T,\mathcal O)$, $F$ and this cover. Its exact sequence contains $$H^d(T,F)\longrightarrow H^d(W,F|_W)\oplus H^d(N,F|_N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}_{W,W\cap N}-\operatorname{res}_{N,W\cap N}}H^d(W\cap N,F|_{W\cap N}).$$ By step 4 the pair $(\xi,0)$ belongs to the kernel of the displayed difference map. Exactness supplies $\widetilde\xi\in H^d(T,F)$ mapping to $(\xi,0)$, whose restriction to $W$ is therefore $\xi$. Since $\xi$ was arbitrary, the restriction in the statement is surjective. The maps here are exactly the section-resolution restrictions specified in the item, by the restriction and difference-map clause of the cited Mayer–Vietoris statement.

The statement is true: it is Stacks 0A3G(2) for O-modules via 01F1(1), with dim<=d, which is no stronger than Stacks because a space of dimension below d has zero H^d on every quasi-compact open. Tested on T or W empty, W=T, and Spec of a rank-one valuation ring with d=1. Step 1: sobriety and dim<=0 make every point closed; det-pe-wlocal-components (1) makes T profinite, so W is clopen and sections glue with zero (the 0A3G base case). Step 2: lem-sfb-ringed-sections-forget-abelian on the site of opens with B=O, K=F[0] is natural in restriction arrows; enough injectives, bounded-below-injective-is-K-injective and restriction of injective resolutions give bijections c_V that commute with restriction. Step 4: lem-weil-pbc-punctured-neighborhood-cohomology-colimit (matches 0A3D(2)) and lem-sc-filtered-colimit-map-zero give N with c_W(xi) zero on N cap W; naturality and injectivity of c pull this back to F. Step 5: lem-sc-mayer-vietoris-ringed-space on T=W cup N lifts (xi,0). No cycle: the dependency closure of 676 nodes does not contain the item.
